subject: Computer Science
text: What is the difference between default parameters and positional parameters? Also give an example of a function header which uses both.
modelAnswer:
Positional parameters are matched to arguments strictly by their position/order in the function call and must always be supplied by the caller. Default parameters have a value assigned in the function header itself, so the caller may omit them, in which case the default value is used.

Example function header using both:
def calc_area(length, width, unit='cm'):
    pass

Here 'length' and 'width' are positional parameters (must be supplied), while 'unit' is a default parameter (optional, defaults to 'cm' if not supplied).
keyPoints: Positional parameters must be passed by the caller, in order.
Default parameters have a value in the header and become optional at the call site.
Default parameters must appear after all positional parameters in the header.
Example: def calc_area(length, width, unit='cm').

text:
What possible output(s) from the given options will NOT be displayed when the following code is executed? Also mention for how many iterations the for loop in the given code will run.
import random
a = [1,2,3,4,5,6]
for i in range(4):
    j = random.randrange(i,5)
    print(a[j],end='-')
print()
Options:
(A) 3-4-5-4-  (B) 2-2-4-5-  (C) 4-3-3-5-  (D) 5-1-2-4-
modelAnswer:
The for loop runs for 4 iterations (i = 0,1,2,3, since range(4) generates 4 values).
In each iteration, j = random.randrange(i,5) picks a random index from i (inclusive) up to 5 (exclusive), i.e. from {i, i+1, i+2, i+3, i+4} intersected with valid indices 0-4 of list a.
So for i=0, j can be 0-4 (a[j] in 1..5); for i=1, j can be 1-4 (a[j] in 2..5); for i=2, j can be 2-4 (a[j] in 3..5); for i=3, j can be 3-4 (a[j] in 4..5).
Since j is always >= i, a[j] (values a[0..4] = 1..5) never equals 6, and more specifically the sequence of printed values must be non-decreasing in their minimum possible index bound each step, meaning the value 1 can only appear in the first print (i=0). Checking option (D) '5-1-2-4-': the second value 1 would require i=1 to allow j=0, but randrange(1,5) can only return 1,2,3 or 4 -- never 0 -- so index 0 (value 1) is impossible once i=1. Hence option (D) 5-1-2-4- will NOT be displayed.
keyPoints: range(4) makes the loop run for exactly 4 iterations.
randrange(i,5) can only return indices from i up to 4 (5 is exclusive).
Because the lower bound i increases each iteration, a[j] cannot revisit indices below i.
Option (D) 5-1-2-4- is impossible because at i=1, index 0 (value 1) is no longer reachable.

modelAnswer:
(a) Advantage: Bus topology requires the least amount of cable, making it simple and cost-effective to set up for a small network. Disadvantage: If the main backbone cable fails or breaks, the entire network goes down.

(b) A protocol is a set of rules and conventions that govern how data is formatted, transmitted and received between devices on a network, so that communication is understood correctly by both sender and receiver. HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used to transmit hypertext across the web.
keyPoints: Bus topology advantage: minimal cabling required, low cost.
Bus topology disadvantage: single point of failure -- a break in the main cable disrupts the whole network.
OR: a protocol is an agreed set of rules for data communication between devices.
OR: HTTP is used to transmit hypertext across the web.

text: NextStep is an organization storing data of Resource Persons in a binary file RESOURCES.DAT, each record a tuple (R_ID, R_Name, R_Expertise, Charges), e.g. (12, 'P. Velusami','Machine Learning',5000). Write the user-defined functions: (i) Append() - to input the data of a Resource Person and write it in the file RESOURCES.DAT. (ii) Update() - to increase the Charges of each resource person by 500.
modelAnswer:
import pickle

def Append():
    f = open("RESOURCES.DAT", "ab")
    r_id = int(input("Enter R_ID: "))
    r_name = input("Enter R_Name: ")
    r_exp = input("Enter R_Expertise: ")
    charges = float(input("Enter Charges: "))
    record = (r_id, r_name, r_exp, charges)
    pickle.dump(record, f)
    f.close()

def Update():
    f = open("RESOURCES.DAT", "rb")
    records = []
    try:
        while True:
            record = pickle.load(f)
            record = (record[0], record[1], record[2], record[3] + 500)
            records.append(record)
    except EOFError:
        pass
    f.close()
    f = open("RESOURCES.DAT", "wb")
    for record in records:
        pickle.dump(record, f)
    f.close()
keyPoints: Append() opens the file in 'ab' (append binary) mode and pickle.dump()s one new record tuple.
Update() reads all existing records with pickle.load() inside a try/except EOFError loop.
Each record's Charges (last field) is increased by 500 while rebuilding the tuple.
The file is reopened in 'wb' mode to rewrite all updated records back.

text: Sanjeevani is setting up Amritsar University Campus with four blocks - ADMIN (25 computers), ACADEMIC (600 computers), HOSTEL (120 computers), SPORTS (50 computers). Block distances: ADMIN-ACADEMIC 60M, ADMIN-HOSTEL 160M, ADMIN-SPORTS 80M, ACADEMIC-HOSTEL 40M, ACADEMIC-SPORTS 120M, HOSTEL-SPORTS 150M. Head office in Hyderabad is 2000 km away. (i) Suggest the most appropriate location of the server inside the campus, and justify. (ii) Suggest the most suitable place/layout to house the switch/hub for each block's cabling. (iii) Name any two wired media to connect computers within a block. (iv) Which communication medium is used by FM: (A) Radio Waves (B) Micro Waves (C) Infrared Waves? [(v)(a) Name the protocol used for audio-visual communication over the internet for online sessions. OR (b) Where should a repeater be installed to boost the signal between blocks? Justify.]
modelAnswer:
(i) The server should be placed in the ACADEMIC block, because it has the maximum number of computers (600), so placing the server there minimizes overall cabling/traffic and gives the most users the fastest access.

(ii) A switch (or hub) should be placed in each of the four blocks (ADMIN, ACADEMIC, HOSTEL, SPORTS) to connect the computers within that block locally, and these switches are then connected to each other (and to the server's block) to form the campus backbone.

(iii) Two wired media: (a) Ethernet cable / Twisted Pair cable (UTP/STP), (b) Coaxial cable (or Optical Fibre Cable).

(iv) (A) Radio Waves -- FM (Frequency Modulation) radio broadcasting uses radio waves for transmission.

(v)(a) VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is used for audio-visual communication over the internet.
OR
(v)(b) A repeater should be installed between ACADEMIC and HOSTEL, since that is the longest single link relative to expected signal-loss thresholds among the frequently used short links, or more generally on any link whose length approaches the maximum cable-run limit (e.g. the ADMIN-HOSTEL link at 160M) to regenerate and boost the weakening signal before it travels further.
keyPoints: Server location: ACADEMIC block, since it has the most computers (600) -- minimizes cabling/latency for the majority.
A switch/hub is placed in every block, then interconnected to form the campus network.
Wired media examples: Ethernet/twisted-pair cable, coaxial cable, optical fibre cable.
FM radio uses Radio Waves (option A); VoIP handles internet audio-visual communication; a repeater goes on a long link (e.g. ADMIN-HOSTEL) to regenerate a weakening signal.

text:
(a) Differentiate between local variable and global variable in Python with an example.
OR
(b) Differentiate between mutable and immutable data types in Python, giving one example of each.
modelAnswer:
(a) A local variable is defined inside a function and is accessible only within that function. A global variable is defined outside all functions and is accessible throughout the program.

Example:
x = 10  # global variable
def demo():
    y = 5  # local variable
    print(x, y)  # both accessible here
demo()
print(x)   # accessible
# print(y)  # would raise NameError — y is local to demo()

OR

(b) Mutable data types can be changed after creation; immutable data types cannot.
Mutable example: List — L = [1,2,3]; L[0] = 99  # modifies in place
Immutable example: Tuple — T = (1,2,3); T[0] = 99  # raises TypeError
keyPoints: Local variable: defined inside a function, accessible only within that function.
Global variable: defined outside functions, accessible throughout the program.
Mutable types can be modified after creation (e.g., list, dict, set).
Immutable types cannot be changed after creation (e.g., int, str, tuple).

text:
(a) Define: (i) Bandwidth (ii) Data Transfer Rate
OR
(b) Differentiate between LAN and WAN giving one example of each.
modelAnswer:
(a)(i) Bandwidth: The maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a network connection in a given amount of time. It is measured in bits per second (bps), Kbps, Mbps, or Gbps.

(ii) Data Transfer Rate: The actual amount of data successfully transferred from one point to another in a given time period. It is the real-world speed of transfer, which may be less than the theoretical bandwidth.

OR

(b) LAN (Local Area Network): A network confined to a small geographic area such as a building or campus. Example: office or school network.

WAN (Wide Area Network): A network spanning a large geographic area, often a country or globally, connecting multiple LANs. Example: The Internet.
keyPoints: Bandwidth: maximum theoretical capacity of a network link.
Data Transfer Rate: actual throughput achieved during transmission.
LAN: small area (building/campus); WAN: large area (city/country/globe).
Internet is the largest example of a WAN.

subject: Computer Science
text:
A binary file 'PASSENGERS.DAT' stores passenger records as dictionaries with keys: PID, PName, Destination, Fare. Write Python functions:
(i) Create() — allows user to input records and write to the binary file.
(ii) SearchDestn(D) — searches and displays all passengers with the given Destination D.
(iii) UpdateFare() — increases Fare by 200 for all passengers and rewrites the file.
modelAnswer:
import pickle

def Create():
    records = []
    while True:
        pid = input('PID: ')
        pname = input('PName: ')
        dest = input('Destination: ')
        fare = int(input('Fare: '))
        records.append({'PID': pid, 'PName': pname, 'Destination': dest, 'Fare': fare})
        if input('Add more? (y/n): ').lower() != 'y':
            break
    with open('PASSENGERS.DAT', 'wb') as f:
        pickle.dump(records, f)

def SearchDestn(D):
    with open('PASSENGERS.DAT', 'rb') as f:
        records = pickle.load(f)
    found = False
    for rec in records:
        if rec['Destination'] == D:
            print(rec)
            found = True
    if not found:
        print('No passengers found for destination', D)

def UpdateFare():
    with open('PASSENGERS.DAT', 'rb') as f:
        records = pickle.load(f)
    for rec in records:
        rec['Fare'] += 200
    with open('PASSENGERS.DAT', 'wb') as f:
        pickle.dump(records, f)
    print('Fares updated successfully')
keyPoints: pickle.dump() writes (serializes) to 'wb' mode; pickle.load() reads from 'rb' mode.
Create(): collect records in a list, dump entire list at once.
SearchDestn(D): load all records, filter by Destination field.
UpdateFare(): load, modify each record's Fare, dump updated list back.
File is rewritten in 'wb' mode after updating fares.

subject: Computer Science
text:
NGO 'Swabhaav' is setting up a network in a new building with four departments: HR (10 computers), Finance (25 computers), Operations (50 computers), Support (15 computers). Distances: HR–Finance 30m, HR–Operations 120m, HR–Support 60m, Finance–Operations 80m, Finance–Support 40m, Operations–Support 90m. A head office in another city is 500 km away.
(i) Which department should house the server? Justify.
(ii) Suggest cabling layout (where to place switches).
(iii) Which department's switch should connect all others? Why?
(iv) Suggest a network protocol to access files securely on the head office server.
(v) Which type of network connects the head office? Name the topology recommended for each department's internal computers.
modelAnswer:
(i) The server should be placed in the Operations department, as it has the most computers (50) — placing the server closest to the largest number of users minimizes access time and network traffic.

(ii) A switch should be placed in each department (HR, Finance, Operations, Support). All departmental switches are connected back to the central switch in Operations (the largest department) to form a Star topology campus backbone.

(iii) The Operations department's switch should act as the central/backbone switch because it has the largest number of computers (50) and is therefore the heaviest traffic node — centralizing connectivity here minimizes hops and latency for most users.

(iv) SSH (Secure Shell) or SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol) should be used for secure remote file access to the head office server. These protocols encrypt data in transit, unlike plain FTP.

(v) The head office connection uses a WAN (Wide Area Network) since it spans 500 km. The recommended internal topology for each department is Star topology — a central switch connects all computers, making fault isolation easy and management simple.
keyPoints: Server location: highest-computer-count department (Operations, 50 computers).
Star topology within each department with a central switch per department.
Operations switch acts as backbone switch — most computers, heaviest traffic.
SSH/SFTP for secure remote file access (encrypted); plain FTP is insecure.
Head office link = WAN; internal cabling = Star topology.

| Circuit Switching | Packet Switching |
|---|---|
| A dedicated communication path is established between sender and receiver for the duration of the session | Data is broken into packets; each packet may take a different route to the destination |
| Resources are reserved for the entire session | Resources are shared; no dedicated path |
| Example: Traditional telephone networks | Example: Internet (TCP/IP) |

Circuit switching: dedicated path, continuous connection
Packet switching: data split into packets, variable routes, shared resources

modelAnswer:
An Alternate Key is a candidate key that was NOT chosen as the primary key. When a table has multiple candidate keys (attributes/combinations that could uniquely identify rows), only one is selected as the primary key — the others become alternate keys.
Example: In a STUDENT table with columns (StudentID, AadharNo, Name, Class): both StudentID and AadharNo can uniquely identify a student. If StudentID is the primary key, then AadharNo is an Alternate Key.
